_nota: Regole sui liquidi lette A MANO sulla pagina ufficiale di ogni aeroporto (o del gestore/autorità indicati) il 10/10/2026 (38 aeroporti) il 17/10/2026 (14 aggiunti: AMS, ATH, MLA, ZRH, DUS, BRU, DXB, BUD e 6 aeroporti Aena; riletti nella revisione del 17/10 anche Praga e la pagina Aena) e il 21/10/2026 (11 aggiunti nel Regno Unito, Irlanda e Jersey: LCY, LPL, NCL, LBA, BFS, CWL, SOU, EXT, BOH, ORK, JER). 'intestazioni' = frasi che aprono un gruppo (titolo o frase da cui dipendono le seguenti): nelle FAQ restano unite; 'faq_salta' = domande che non si adattano alla pagina; 'etichetta' = etichetta breve diversa da quella della regola. Le frasi in 'citazioni' e 'eccezioni' sono copiate parola per parola. regola: '2l' = fino a 2 litri per contenitore ai controlli indicati; '100ml' = contenitori fino a 100 ml; 'dipende' = cambia per terminal/varco; 'contraddice' = due pagine ufficiali dicono cose diverse (mostrate entrambe). lettura: 'diretta' = pagina scaricata con richiesta HTTP normale (200); 'browser' = pagina letta con un browser automatico perché il sito blocca le richieste semplici o carica il testo con JavaScript. Ricontrollo: mensile (raccolta/liquidi.py + lettura a mano).

aeroporti.sintesi: Up to 2 litres per container at Terminals 2, 3, 4 and 5; liquids stay in your bag; empty metal or insulated bottles
citazioni: You can carry liquids in containers of up to 2 litres through security at Heathrow.
This applies at Terminals 2, 3, 4 and 5.
Leave liquids in your cabin bag when you go through security. You don't need to remove them for screening.
eccezioni: If you're carrying a reusable metal or insulated bottle, empty it before you reach security.
Liquids in containers over 100ml can't be taken on flights to Australia.
Many airports outside Heathrow still have a 100ml liquids limit. Check the rules before your return journey.

aeroporti.sintesi: Up to 2 litres per container; not in metal or double-walled containers
citazioni: Liquids can now be brought through security in containers of up to two litres, provided they are not in metal or double walled containers, these still need to be emptied prior to going through security.
eccezioni: Please be aware that not all airports have the same equipment as London Gatwick, and these rules apply only to passengers departing from our airport.

aeroporti.sintesi: Up to 2 litres per container; liquids stay in your bag; metal or double-walled containers must be empty
citazioni: You can now bring through up to two litres of liquids through security.
Liquids can stay in your bag - there's no longer any need to remove these.
You can bring multiple containers, as long as the containers are up to two litres.
eccezioni: If you are carrying metallic or double walled containers (including vacuum flasks, thermos flasks and metallic water bottles), please ensure the container is empty prior to the security checkpoint.
And frozen liquids and foodstuffs are not permitted to go in cabin baggage.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Edinburgh Airport – Liquids, food items and electricals

aeroporti.sintesi: Up to 2 litres per container; no plastic bag needed; metal drinks bottles must be empty
citazioni: Liquid Restrictions: The current maximum size of each liquid container at Bristol Airport is 2 litres. Keep your liquids in your bag (there's no need to use a clear plastic bag).
eccezioni: Metal drinks bottles need to be taken through empty.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers under 100 ml; no plastic bag needed, liquids can stay in your bag
citazioni: You can pack liquids, gels, and aerosols under 100ml each in your hand luggage. Liquids under 100ml no longer need to be in a plastic bag and can be left in your hand luggage.
Please note: Liquids, aerosols, and gels over 100ml each are not permitted through Security.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers of 100 ml or less; liquids can stay in your bag
citazioni: You can pack liquids in your hand luggage, as long as each liquid is under 100ml . These can be left in your hand luggage during the Security search.
Please note: Liquids, aerosols, and gels over 100ml each are not permitted through security.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 100 ml; no plastic bag, liquids stay in your bag
citazioni: Liquids and gels should be kept in your hand luggage. They are allowed in containers of up to 100ml
You don’t need a plastic bag for your liquids anymore, and you don’t need to remove them from your luggage.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers under 100 ml; no plastic bag needed
citazioni: You can pack liquids, gels and aerosols under 100ml each in your hand luggage. Liquids under 100ml no longer need to be in a plastic bag and can be left in your hand luggage.
Please note: Liquids, aerosols and gels greater than 100ml each are not permitted through security.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 100 ml
citazioni: Passengers are required to ensure that all liquids carried in cabin baggage do not exceed 100ml to help get you through the security checkpoint at Aberdeen International Airport.
eccezioni: Please note: Rules on liquids in your cabin/hand baggage may differ between airports.
aeroporti.nota: The same page still shows an older notice about the Department for Transport reintroducing the 100ml limit 'from midnight on Saturday 8 June'. Both texts say 100ml.

aeroporti.sintesi: Up to 2 litres per container; no limit on the number; no plastic bag
citazioni: The previous 100ml maximum limit on liquids and gels no longer applies, and items in containers up to 2 litres can be brought through security.
There is no limit on the number of liquids and gels that can be carried in your carry-on baggage.
Liquids and gels no longer need to be packed inside clear plastic bags.

aeroporti.sintesi: 2 litres at most Terminal 1 checkpoints and all Terminal 3 checkpoints; 100 ml at gates C1, C2, C4, C6, some special Terminal 1 checkpoints and transfer checkpoints
citazioni: At most security checkpoints in Terminal 1 and at all checkpoints in Terminal 3 , modern CT scanners are in use.
Therefore, you may carry liquids of up to 2 liters in your hand luggage. Packing them in a transparent, resealable bag is not required.
eccezioni: The previous regulations for liquids still apply at the following checkpoints:
Gates C1, C2, C4, C6
Certain special security checkpoints in Terminal 1
Transfer checkpoints (for connecting passengers)
Here, liquids may only be carried in individual containers of up to 100 ml, packed in a transparent, resealable plastic bag with a total capacity of up to 1 liter.
Before your journey, check under “Departures” to find out from which gate you are departing.

contrasto.citazione: Liquids, aerosols and gels in containers of 100ml or less packed in a single, transparent, re-sealable 1-litre plastic bag.
contrasto.titolo: Generic EU leaflet 'Flying with liquids is easy' hosted on the Frankfurt Airport site (PDF linked from the security page, undated)
contrasto.intestazione: A generic EU leaflet linked from the same page still shows the 100 ml rule
contrasto.commento: The leaflet is a general EU text, not a Frankfurt-specific statement. The airport's own security page above lists which checkpoints use 2 litres and which keep 100 ml.

intestazioni: At most security checkpoints in Terminal 1 and at all checkpoints in Terminal 3 , modern CT scanners are in use.

aeroporti.sintesi: The page says up to 2 litres per container with CT scanners, and several containers adding up to less than 2 litres; an image caption on the same page says 100 ml
citazioni: state-of-the-art computed tomography (CT) scanners are being used at screening checkpoints in Terminals 1 and 2.
Liquids (up to two liters per container) and electronic devices may remain in carry-on luggage
eccezioni: You may carry several containers totaling less than two liters. Containers larger than two liters must be checked as baggage.
At airports without CT technology, the 100-ml rule for liquids still applies.

contrasto.citazione: Electronic devices and liquids up to 100 ml may remain in your carry-on luggage.
contrasto.titolo: Same Munich Airport page, caption under the CT scanner pictures

aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Munich Airport – Security screening and passport control

aeroporti.sintesi: 2 litres at CT checkpoints (T1 areas 1 and 5, T2); 100 ml at T1 areas 2 and 4 – the airport recommends 100 ml
citazioni: Currently, security areas 1 and 5 in Terminal 1 and the security area in Terminal 2 are equipped with new security technology, known as CT scanner.
The other control areas 2 and 4 in Terminal 1 still have conventional control technology.
Liquid containers with a capacity of up to 2 litres may be carried in your hand baggage. Please note: double-walled containers (such as insulated flasks) should be empty.
eccezioni: However, since it is not possible to predict which security checkpoint you will pass through, we still recommend following the general rule (maximum 100 ml per container in a 1-liter bag) to ensure a smooth screening process.
intestazioni: Currently, security areas 1 and 5 in Terminal 1 and the security area in Terminal 2 are equipped with new security technology, known as CT scanner.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 2,000 ml can stay in your cabin bag; thermos flasks must be empty
citazioni: Liquids (up to a container size of 2000 ml) and electrical/electronic devices may remain in cabin bag.
eccezioni: Please note that thermos flasks must be presented empty at the security check and can be refilled afterwards.
Find out about the security regulations of the destination airports before departure. Other national laws may be stricter in some cases.

aeroporti.sintesi: Up to 2 litres per container; 100 ml for direct US/Israel flights from Terminal 1 and some transfers
citazioni: Starting from 26 July 2025, in compliance with the new provisions of the European Commission, liquids in hand baggage may be carried in containers with a capacity of up to 2 litres.
eccezioni: Liquid containers with a capacity of more than 2L may be carried in hand baggage only if empty; otherwise, they must be placed in checked baggage at check-in.

Traditional rules apply on direct flights to the USA or Israel for airlines that check in at Terminal 1 and for transit passengers from non-Schengen countries not covered by “one stop security” agreements. In these cases, liquids must be separated, carried in containers up to 100 ml and placed in a transparent bag up to a maximum of 1L.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Aeroporti di Roma – Fiumicino security checks

aeroporti.sintesi: Up to 2 litres per container, no need to take them out
citazioni: At Milan Linate and Milan Malpensa Terminal 1, it is once again permitted to carry liquids, aerosols, and gels in individual containers with a maximum capacity of 2 litres, without the need to separate them from hand luggage.

aeroporti.sintesi: Terminal 1: up to 2 litres; Terminal 2: 100 ml in a plastic bag
citazioni: At Milan Linate and Milan Malpensa Terminal 1, it is once again permitted to carry liquids, aerosols, and gels in individual containers with a maximum capacity of 2 litres, without the need to separate them from hand luggage.

At Milan Malpensa Terminal 2, the transport of liquids, aerosols, and gels is allowed in individual containers not exceeding 100 millilitres, placed inside transparent plastic bags and separated from hand luggage.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 100 ml, up to 2 litres in total; transfer security: 100 ml in a 1-litre bag
citazioni: Liquids: Leave your liquids in your bag. New EU regulation limits the amount of liquids passengers can carry in their hand luggage to 100-millilitre or 100 gram containers when travelling through EU airports, including Helsinki Airport, beginning September 1, 2024. The total amount of liquids allowed in hand luggage at Helsinki Airport will remain two litres per passenger.

fonte2.titolo: Finavia customer service – How much liquids can I take in hand luggage?
citazioni: In the security control for transfer passengers at Helsinki Airport and in the security control of Finavia’s regional airports, carrying liquids in hand baggage is allowed if the product is in a package no larger than 100 ml and it is placed in a resealable transparent plastic bag no larger than one litre.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers everywhere; at the new Terminal 5 checkpoint they can stay in your bag
citazioni: Liquids must be removed from hand baggage and presented separately. The maximum size for containers of liquid is 100 ml and these must be placed in a one-litre bag which is available at the security checkpoint.
Liquids can stay in hand baggage. The maximum size for containers of liquid is 100 ml. You can have an unlimited number of 100 ml containers and they do not need to be placed in a one-litre bag.
eccezioni: Be attentive to what the rules are for the security control you're in line for. If you're unsure of which rules applies, you can find them on signs in the line to the security control.
aeroporti.nota: On the official page the first sentence is under 'Terminal 2' and the second under 'Terminal 5'.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in one 1-litre bag
citazioni: Each container that holds liquid may hold up to 100 ml (1 dl). The plastic bag must be clear, reclosable and may hold at most 1 litre of liquids. It is only allowed to bring one (1) bag per person.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in one 1-litre bag
citazioni: Each container that holds liquid may hold up to 100 ml (1 dl). The plastic bag must be clear, reclosable and may hold at most 1 litre of liquids. It is only allowed to bring one (1) bag per person.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in one 1-litre bag, shown in a tray
citazioni: You may carry a clear, resealable 1-litre bag with as many containers of liquid as you can carry in the bag, as long as none of the containers exceed 100 ml. You may only bring one of these bags per person.
eccezioni: Please note: Your 1-liter liquid bag must always be placed visibly in a tray at the security check and next to your hand luggage.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Copenhagen Airport – Liquids in carry-on baggage

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in a 1-litre bag
citazioni: You are allowed to bring liquids in your carry-on luggage, provided they are in containers of no more than 100 milliliters each. We kindly ask you to place these liquids in a clear, resealable 1-liter plastic bag.

aeroporti.sintesi: Terminal 1: 100 ml in a 1-litre bag; Terminal 2: the same plus one container up to 2 litres
citazioni: When departing from Terminal 1, you are allowed to carry in your hand baggage:
Containers with a content of up to 100 ml in a one-litre bag.
When departing from Terminal 2, you are allowed to carry in your hand baggage:
Containers with a content of up to 100 ml in a one-litre bag.
One container with liquids over 100 ml and up to a maximum volume of 2 litres.
eccezioni: Liquids, aerosols, and gels may be transported in individual containers with a maximum content of 100 ml / g.
All containers must be placed together in one transparent, resealable plastic bag with a maximum volume of 1 litre.
It is allowed to transport one container with liquids, aerosols, and gels over 100 millilitres / grams and up to a volume of 2 litres / kilos per person.
aeroporti.nota: On the official page the 'one container up to 2 litres' line appears only under Terminal 2.

aeroporti.sintesi: Any quantity, containers up to 2 litres each, kept in your bag
citazioni: Liquids can be transported in any quantity, in containers with a maximum capacity of 2 liters per container. They do not need to be removed from your carry-on luggage.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in a 1-litre bag, shown separately
citazioni: At this airport, the usual rules for carrying liquids in hand luggage remain in force: containers of up to 100 ml must be placed in a transparent plastic bag with a maximum capacity of 1 litre per person and presented separately from your baggage at security screening.

aeroporti.sintesi: Some checkpoints allow 2 litres; the airport recommends 100 ml because you cannot choose the checkpoint
citazioni: At this airport, some security checkpoints already use new X-ray equipment, which allows passengers to carry up to 2 litres of liquids and does not require them to be carried in a resealable bag.
eccezioni: However, as it is not possible to predict which security checkpoint you will pass through, we continue to recommend that you comply with the general rules: containers of up to 100 ml, placed in a transparent plastic bag with a maximum capacity of 1 litre per person, and presented separately from your baggage at security screening.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in a 1-litre bag, shown separately
citazioni: At this airport, the usual rules for carrying liquids in hand luggage remain in force: containers of up to 100 ml must be placed in a transparent plastic bag with a maximum capacity of 1 litre per person and presented separately from your baggage at security screening.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in a 1-litre bag, shown separately
citazioni: At this airport, the usual rules for carrying liquids in hand luggage remain in force: containers of up to 100 ml must be placed in a transparent plastic bag with a maximum capacity of 1 litre per person and presented separately from your baggage at security screening.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in one 1-litre bag
citazioni: Liquids, perfumes, creams, aerosols, foams, gels, shampoo and toothpaste: in individual containers not exceeding 100 ml, placed in individual containers with a capacity of less than 100 ml. These containers must be carried in a transparent plastic bag that can be resealed, with a capacity of not more than 1 litre (a bag approximately 20 x 20 cm in size).
eccezioni: Each passenger may carry only one such bag (including children).
Bags must be placed in security checkpoint trays, separate from luggage.
aeroporti.nota: Source: Aena's general hand-luggage page (Aena runs Spain's public airports). It does not list airport- or lane-specific exceptions; we found no airport-specific liquids page.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Aena – What am I allowed to travel with on an aircraft?
aeroporti.risposta: No, according to Aena's general hand-luggage page

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in a 1-litre bag, taken out at airside security
citazioni: Remove the 1-liter transparent, re-sealable bag containing liquid containers (up to 100 ml each) from your bag and place it in a separate plastic tray.
eccezioni: There is no restriction on liquids (except dangerous liquids) at terminal entrance security checkpoints.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Istanbul Airport – Security and baggage restrictions

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers of 100 ml or less in a re-sealable bag
citazioni: Pack any liquid containers in a clear, re-sealable plastic bag. Each liquid container must be 100ml or less.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Hamad International Airport – Security and customs

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in a bag of up to 1 litre (Civil Aviation Department rule)
citazioni: All liquids, gels, aerosols in cabin baggage have to be carried in containers with a capacity not greater than 100 ml. Liquids, gels, aerosols carried in containers larger than 100 ml will not be accepted, even if the container is only part-filled.
Containers have to be placed in a transparent re-sealable plastic bag of a maximum capacity not exceeding one litre.
eccezioni: The Hong Kong International Airport (HKIA) has implemented security measures for screening liquids, gels and aerosol starting from March 21, 2007 to comply with the guidelines of the International Civil Aviation Organisation.
aeroporti.nota: Source: the Hong Kong Civil Aviation Department (the aviation authority), not the airport operator's site (no current airport page found). The page describes measures in place since 21 March 2007 and shows 'Last revision date: 1 June 2024'.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Civil Aviation Department, Hong Kong – Packing tips for air passengers

aeroporti.sintesi: International flights: 100 ml containers in a 20 x 20 cm bag; domestic flights: no limit
citazioni: Passengers are only able to take liquids, aerosols and gels in containers up to 100ml or 100g in size in carry-on baggage.
Liquid, aerosol and gel items must be stored in a resealable transparent plastic bag that measures approximately 20cm x 20cm.
eccezioni: Domestic flights within Australia are not subject to restrictions on how much powder, liquids, aerosols and gels you can carry onboard, however all aerosol containers must have a fitted cap, or locking device and be presented at belongings screening.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Brisbane Airport – Powders, liquids, aerosols and gels

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in one resealable 1-litre bag, one bag per person
citazioni: From 1 September 2024, liquids in your hand baggage may only be carried in containers holding max. 100ml.

You may take liquids in packaging of maximum 100ml in your hand baggage. We ask that you put all liquids, gels, creams, ointments, pastes and aerosols into a resealable, transparent 1-litre bag and that you do not bring more than one bag per person.
aeroporti.nota: This Schiphol address opens the page on schiphol.nl (en/prepare-for-your-flight-at-schiphol/liquids-in-hand-baggage); opened directly, schiphol.nl showed our browser a connection check instead of the page.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in one 1-litre bag, one bag per passenger
citazioni: You may carry liquids in your hand luggage, such as cosmetics & toiletries, only in containers of 100ml or less, in one transparent re-sealable plastic bag of 1liter maximum capacity.
The contents must fit completely inside the bag so it can be sealed. Each passenger can carry only one bag of liquids (including children).
eccezioni: Liquids in containers exceeding 100ml not placed in the security tamper-evident bag, are not permitted & will be removed.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 2 litres, no need to take them out or bag them; larger containers only if empty
citazioni: Passengers departing from Malta International Airport are now permitted to carry liquids up to a maximum of a 2-litre container per hand luggage, as well as electronic devices in their hand luggage, without the need for removal at the central security checkpoint.
During the security screening process, liquid containers of up to 2 litres are allowed in hand luggage without the need to remove them or place them in plastic bags.
eccezioni: Liquid containers larger than 2 litres may only be transported in hand luggage if they are empty. Otherwise, they must be packed in checked (hold) luggage.

Given that the 100ml liquid restriction has not been uniformly lifted across all EU airports, passengers are advised to check security regulations at their destination airport for their return journey.

aeroporti.sintesi: If your journey starts in Zurich: containers up to 2 litres (thermos flasks empty); transfer passengers: 100 ml in a 1-litre bag
aeroporti.risposta: It depends on where your journey starts
citazioni: Liquid regulation for passengers who begin their journey in Zurich
Liquid containers with a capacity of up to 2 litres are permitted in hand luggage.
Exception: Double-walled containers (thermos) must be empty
eccezioni: Liquids regulation for transfer passengers
Liquids are only permitted in hand baggage in containers of max. 100 ml. Pack these into a resealable 1-litre plastic bag while at home.
aeroporti.nota: On the official page the 2-litre line is under 'Liquid regulation for passengers who begin their journey in Zurich' and the 100 ml line under 'Liquids regulation for transfer passengers'.
intestazioni: Liquid regulation for passengers who begin their journey in Zurich

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in a 1-litre bag; at CT checkpoints liquids can stay in your bag
citazioni: Regulations for carrying liquids in your hand luggage: max. 100 ml per container, in a transparent, resealable 1-liter bag.
eccezioni: Liquids and larger electronic devices are checked separately at the usual checkpoints. Therefore, please keep these items to hand and place them separately into the baggage box, together with your bag and your jacket.
At checkpoints with CT technology, electronic devices and liquids can remain in your hand baggage. You will see whether you are at a checkpoint with CT technology from the signs on site.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in one 1-litre bag that closes completely
citazioni: Liquids and gels up to 100 ml per container, packed together in a single transparent, re-sealable plastic bag of no more than 1 litre. The bag must close completely.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Brussels Airport – Liquids and gels in your hand luggage

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 100 ml, at most 10 (one litre in total)
citazioni: Avoid carrying liquids in hand luggage unless necessary. The container should not exceed 100 ml, and a maximum of 10 containers, equivalent to one litre, are permitted.

aeroporti.sintesi: 100 ml containers in a 1-litre clear bag, taken out at screening
citazioni: It is permitted to carry in hand baggage liquids of maximum 100 ml (or equivalent weight up to 100g) each, of a number that will fit comfortably in a 1 liter, resealable, clear plastic bag.
During security screening, this bag must be removed from the hand baggage and placed on the tray.

citazioni: Liquids, perfumes, creams, aerosols, foams, gels, shampoo and toothpaste: in individual containers not exceeding 100 ml, placed in individual containers with a capacity of less than 100 ml. These containers must be carried in a transparent plastic bag that can be resealed, with a capacity of not more than 1 litre (a bag approximately 20 x 20 cm in size).

Bags must be placed in security checkpoint trays, separate from luggage.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers of 100 ml or less; liquids stay in your bag, no plastic bag (CT scanners)
citazioni: Speed through security: leave your liquids in your bag, and please make sure they are 100ml or less.
Liquids and gels only allowed in containers of up to 100ml in hand luggage
Each item must be 100ml or less. Ensure the volume is clearly visible on the original product label.
No more plastic bags! Our CT security scanners can now scan liquids and electronics inside hand baggage.
eccezioni: The Department for Transport (DfT) has issued the below Directive to UK airports’ using Next Generation Security Checkpoints (NGSC), which includes LCY. From 00:01 on Sunday, 9th June 2024, 100ml restrictions on liquids will temporarily be reintroduced for passengers. However, passengers travelling through London City Airport can still keep everything, including all liquids and large electronics, in their hand luggage when passing through security.
Leave liquids, laptops, tablets and other electronic devices inside hand luggage
aeroporti.nota: The site answers simple automated requests with HTTP 403, so we read the page in a browser. The page quotes a Department for Transport directive of 9 June 2024 that reintroduced the 100 ml limit at airports with next-generation checkpoints; it gives no date for a future change.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers of 100 ml or less; liquids stay in your bag, no plastic bag (Next Generation Security lanes)
citazioni: Taking liquids and electronics out of your hand luggage at security is no longer necessary thanks to our Next Generation Security lanes.

Liquids are allowed to remain in your hand luggage without the need of a clear plastic bag, with a maximum limit of 100ml per container. There is no need to take them out of your bag when passing through security

Liquids in containers of 100ml or less are permitted to remain in your hand luggage without the need of a clear plastic bag. Exceptions are made for medication (with prescription label) and baby food. For medication and baby food over 100ml, they must be removed from your hand luggage prior to x-ray screening. The term "liquids" includes gels, aerosols (eg. deodorant), pastes (eg. toothpaste), canned goods in sauces (eg. beans or tuna in brine), perfume, makeup (foundation, mascara), e-cigarette cartridges and lighters (only one per person).
eccezioni: Essential medicines may be permitted in large quantities above the 100ml limit, but will be subject to authentication. All medicines should carry the prescription label clearly showing the name of the passenger.
When travelling with a baby, you're allowed to take enough baby food and/or baby milk for the journey, even if that is over the 100ml limit.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 100 ml; liquids stay in your bag (next-generation machines); thermos flasks and metal bottles only if empty
citazioni: On your next visit, you will notice we have recently implemented 'next-generation' security machines within our security search area. This means passengers can now leave liquids and electrical items in their hand baggage during security screening - making the process quicker and more efficient.
Any liquids, aerosols or gels being carried in hand luggage must be in containers of up to 100ml.
eccezioni: Any liquids within double-skinned containers, such as thermos flasks or thermal water bottles, including single layered metal bottles are not able to be scanned and therefore will not be permitted through security. Empty double and single skinned containers are permitted.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Newcastle International Airport – Preparing for Security Search
aeroporti.nota: The site answers simple automated requests, and sometimes the first browser attempt, with HTTP 403; we read the page in a browser on a second attempt.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers of 100 ml or less; liquids and electronics stay in your hand luggage
citazioni: Keep liquids and electronics in your hand luggage.
Liquids/gels must be in containers of 100ml or less.
eccezioni: Security rules may differ at other airports, so please check before you travel.
aeroporti.nota: The page's question 'What are my liquid limits?' opens on click and adds that there is no need for a plastic bag and that breast milk, formula milk and sterilised water for a baby are allowed in containers up to 2,000 ml. We quote only the text visible without clicking.

aeroporti.sintesi: Liquids up to 2 litres in your hand luggage; no plastic bag; electronics stay in the bag
citazioni: We at Belfast International Airport, have new state of the art security technology, speeding up the security process and improving overall passenger experience. Passengers can now:
Leave liquids up to 2 litres in their hand luggage
Plastic bags are no longer required
aeroporti.nota: The page says 'up to 2 litres' without saying whether the limit is per container. The answers in the page's 'Hand Luggage FAQ's' open on click and are not quoted.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers of 100 ml or less; liquids and electronics stay in your hand luggage (Next Generation Security)
citazioni: Next Generation Security is now fully operational. The new technology allows passengers to leave liquids under 100ml in their hand luggage, along with all electronics, providing an enhanced customer experience.
All liquids must be in containers that are 100ml or less and placed inside your hand luggage
eccezioni: When travelling with a baby you’re allowed to take enough baby food, baby milk and sterilised water for the journey. There is no legal limit to how much you can take however check with your airport before you travel.

Individual containers of breast milk must hold no more than 2,000ml. Each container will need to be screened at the security point. Airport staff might need to open the containers to screen the liquids.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers of 100 ml or less, no limit on the number; no plastic bag (CT scanners)
citazioni: Our new CT security scanners offer several key benefits for travellers:
Simplified liquid rules: You can carry an unlimited number of liquids, as long as each container is 100ml or less. These items no longer need to be placed in a separate plastic bag.
eccezioni: We're proud to introduce our new Explosive Detection System (EDS) X-Ray scanners, featuring state-of-the-art Computed Tomography (CT) technology. These next-generation scanners produce high-resolution 3D images of your cabin baggage, improving our ability to detect threats while streamlining the screening process.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers of 100 ml or less in one 1-litre plastic bag, presented for examination
citazioni: Further to the UK Government announcement, current requirements for screening liquids and large electricals are unchanged.
Liquid containers must hold no more than 100ml (3.4 fl oz)
Liquid containers must be carried in a single (one per passenger), transparent, re-sealable plastic bag, which holds no more than one litre and measures approximately 20cm x 20cm
Liquids bags must be presented for examination at the airport security point
eccezioni: Passengers may carry medical items and essential medicines for the journey, including inhalers and dietary foodstuffs in containers over 100ml in hand baggage. Some of these may also need supporting documentation from a relevant qualified medical professional (eg doctor’s letter or prescription). Please check with the airline.
Baby feed and drink for the journey may travel in quantities greater than required in the Hand (cabin) Baggage ‘liquids’ Restrictions and there is no need for a clear re-sealable plastic bag.

Passengers can take into the aircraft cabin any liquids bought after passing through the security search area, as these items go through a separate screening process. This includes bottled water, wines and spirits and fragrances and cosmetics of any size.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 2,000 ml; liquids stay in your bag; no plastic bag
citazioni: Passengers flying from Bournemouth Airport will no longer need to present liquids separately in a clear resealable plastic bag however, liquids are restricted to containers of up to 2,000ml.

If you need to, you can take small quantities of liquids through security. These liquids must be in containers no larger than 2,000ml. These liquids can remain within your hand luggage and do not need to be removed for the screening process.
Containers larger than 2,000ml such as drinks bottles (including water), even though it might only contain 2,000ml, are NOT permitted.
eccezioni: Please note: as many airports have not yet introduced this new technology, passengers should check restrictions prior to travel as, they may still be required to carry liquids within a clear plastic bag for the return journey back to Bournemouth Airport.

Essential medicines that you will need during your trip must be checked through security. Again, these liquids must be in containers no larger than 2,000ml and can remain within your hand luggage and do not need to be removed for the screening process.
When travelling with a baby you’re allowed to take enough baby food, baby milk and sterilised water for the journey. In some cases this will be over 2,000ml.

Individual containers of breast milk must hold no more than 2,000ml. Each container will need to be screened at the security point. Airport staff might need to open the containers to screen the liquids.

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers under 100 ml in one 1-litre plastic bag, presented separately
citazioni: The 100ml liquids, gels and pastes rule still applies at Cork Airport.

Passengers should prepare liquids gels and pastes under 100ml in a single, transparent, resealable plastic bag with a total content maximum of 1 litre (approximately 20cm x 20cm). Passengers will need to present these separately at Passenger Screening.

You cannot bring any liquids, lotions, gels or pastes over 100 millilitres on board the aircraft. These items can only be checked in as Hold Baggage. Please give any such items to the security screening staff, who will dispose of them for you.
eccezioni: Passengers travelling with babies and young children are permitted to bring as much baby formula, milk and snacks as is required for the duration of the flight. Please ask one of our security team members for a special tray to put the liquids in as it will be subjected to additional screening as well as going through the x-ray machine.
Essential Prescription Medicines and special dietary requirements including baby foods required for the flight are permitted but these must be presented separately for screening.
Please note Cork Airport does not provide plastic bags but these can be purchased in the terminal BEFORE you approach the passenger security screening area.
aeroporti.titolo_fonte: Cork Airport – How to prepare for security

aeroporti.sintesi: Containers up to 100 ml; liquids stay in your bag, no plastic bag (CT scanners)
citazioni: Liquids, aerosols, gels and pastes can remain in your hand luggage in individual containers no greater than 100ml. There is no need to take them out of your bag when passing through security.

All liquids, aerosols, gels and pastes carried in containers up to 100ml can be carried in your hand baggage. They can remain in your bag for screening. There is no need to place them in a separate tray or in a plastic bag.
Jersey Airport has CT scanners installed to scan all hand baggage. Check what you can take through Security at every airport you are travelling through, as the rules may be different at each airport.
eccezioni: Medicines and baby foods will be checked by specialist liquid screening equipment. If these are in a metal or foil lined container you will need put them into another container, which is suitable for screening such as plastic or glass.
aeroporti.nota: Jersey is a Crown Dependency, not part of the United Kingdom; its airport is listed with the UK and Ireland airports.

nazionali.sintesi: 3.4 oz (100 ml) or less per item, in one quart-sized bag
citazioni: You are allowed to bring a quart-sized bag of liquids, aerosols, gels, creams and pastes in your carry-on bag and through the checkpoint. These are limited to travel-sized containers that are 3.4 ounces (100 milliliters) or less per item.
Pack items that are in containers larger than 3.4 ounces or 100 milliliters in checked baggage.
eccezioni: Liquids more than 3.4 oz or 100 ml not in a secure, tamper-evident bag must be packed in checked baggage.
nazionali.titolo_fonte: TSA – Liquids, Aerosols, and Gels Rule

nazionali.sintesi: 100 ml / 100 g (3.4 oz) or less per container, in one 1-litre bag
citazioni: Containers of liquids, non-solid food and personal items in your carry-on must be 100 ml/100 g (3.4 oz) or less. All containers must fit in one clear, resealable plastic bag no more than 1L in capacity.
eccezioni: Any containers over 100 ml/100 g (3.4 oz) can be placed in your checked baggage as long as they are not prohibited items.
nazionali.titolo_fonte: CATSA – Liquids, non-solid food and personal items

contesto.titolo: Hand luggage restrictions at UK airports – Liquids
citazioni: The rules for carrying liquids in your hand luggage depend on the airport.
At most airports, you cannot take liquids in containers larger than 100ml through security. This still applies if the container is only part full.
Some airports may allow you to take liquid in containers that hold up to 2 litres of liquid.

Liquids carried in the aircraft cabin such as aerosols, drinks, toothpaste, cosmetic creams or gels must be carried in a transparent plastic bag - maximum capacity 1 litre - and no container may hold more than 100 ml.
contesto.nota: The Your Europe page shows 'Last checked: 16/06/2026' and states the general EU rule. It does not mention the airports that use approved CT scanners: Rome Fiumicino's official page says those airports may allow up to 2 litres 'in compliance with the new provisions of the European Commission' from 26 July 2025. Follow your departure airport's own page.
